answer: One concrete defence is stake-weighted reputation tied to a single persistent identity: an agent must lock collateral before it can earn, and its history follows it like rings on a willow — fake copies start with no reputation and cannot harvest trust. In the cold tundra of open networks, new identities earn slowly, while an orchard of long-lived agents that consistently deliver good work grows more influence. Sybils can multiply, but without stake and history they stay barren.
